content.user_title: Learn Robotics Concepts with Clear Guidance
content.value_statement: Robotics learners need clear explanations across ROS 2, simulation, and Physical AI. This skill provides a focused reference for core concepts and troubleshooting discussions.
actual_capabilities: Explains ROS 2 as robotics middleware and identifies ROS 2 Humble as the referenced version.
Explains inverse kinematics, SLAM, reinforcement learning, and computer vision for robotics.
Describes the roles of Isaac Sim and Gazebo in robotics simulation.
Provides conceptual guidance for Python and C++ robotics control work.
Helps structure learning around modules, labs, and a capstone project.
Supports clear discussions of humanoid robotics and embodied intelligence.
limitations: It provides domain guidance, not a complete ROS 2 implementation or project repository.
It does not execute simulations, control physical hardware, or validate sensor data.
It does not replace hardware safety procedures, testing, or expert review.
Its ROS 2 reference is limited to the Humble Hawksbill version named in the skill.

use_cases.title: Prepare a robotics study plan
use_cases.description: Organize introductory study topics around ROS 2, perception, planning, and simulation.

use_cases.title: Clarify simulation concepts
use_cases.description: Compare Isaac Sim and Gazebo before selecting a simulator for a learning exercise.

use_cases.title: Discuss a humanoid prototype
use_cases.description: Review core concepts such as inverse kinematics, SLAM, and perception for a prototype discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a core concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain inverse kinematics in simple terms. Include one practical humanoid robotics example.

prompt_templates.title: Compare simulators
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Isaac Sim and Gazebo for a ROS 2 learner. Describe the role of each simulator.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a ROS 2 exercise
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short ROS 2 Humble lab outline for learning robot perception. Include objectives and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a simulation issue
prompt_templates.prompt: I am simulating a mobile robot that loses its estimated position. Explain how SLAM, sensor quality, and simulation assumptions could affect the result.

output_examples.output: SLAM helps a robot build a map while estimating its own position. It combines sensor observations with movement estimates as the robot explores.

output_examples.input: What is the difference between Isaac Sim and Gazebo?
output_examples.output: Isaac Sim is a photorealistic NVIDIA simulation environment. Gazebo is an open-source 3D robotics simulator commonly used for robotics development and learning.

output: Build a simulated mobile robot that detects objects and creates a map.
Use ROS 2 concepts to connect perception, localization, and navigation discussions.
Define measurable simulation tests before presenting results.

best_practices: State the robot platform, simulator, ROS 2 version, and learning goal before asking for guidance.
Validate conceptual advice in a simulation before applying it to physical hardware.
Use hardware safety procedures and expert review for any real robot deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not treat conceptual guidance as a tested hardware control solution.
Do not omit sensor assumptions when discussing SLAM or computer vision results.
Do not apply simulation results to a physical robot without validation and safety checks.

faq.question: What robotics topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Physical AI, ROS 2, humanoid robotics, simulation, inverse kinematics, SLAM, reinforcement learning, and computer vision.

faq.question: Which ROS 2 version does it reference?
faq.answer: The skill references ROS 2 Humble Hawksbill.

faq.question: Can it run Isaac Sim or Gazebo?
faq.answer: No. It explains their roles and can support troubleshooting discussions, but it does not run simulators.

faq.question: Can it control a real robot?
faq.answer: No. It provides educational guidance and does not operate hardware.

faq.question: Can it provide ROS 2 code examples?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the agent to help with ROS 2 examples in Python and C++. Review and test examples before use.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful for beginners who need clear explanations of foundational robotics concepts.
